UPDATE: FIREWORKS
RESPONSE FROM POLICE AND COUNCIL


**
------------------------------------------------------------
Dear Requester

Fireworks continue to cause unacceptable noise disturbances in our community.

I raised the issue at Full Council on Monday, emphasising the importance of both the Council and the Police working together.

You can watch my comments here.  (https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1JExrTZK3w/)

https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1JExrTZK3w/

On Wednesday, our village experienced another incident.

It is clear neither the police nor the Vale of Glamorgan Council have taken sufficient action to date to address this problem.

Both authorities have failed to fulfill their duties to protect our community.

I've written to both authorities to raise serious concerns.

You can read my letter below.
FAO: South Wales Police
Vale of Glamorgan Council

8th October 2026


Dear both

Illegal firework usage in Llandough

I’m saddened to report that another firework related incident took place in Llandough last night.

This is impacting some of the most vulnerable members of our community, causing distress to the elderly, small children and animals.

It is apparent that those responsible for setting off fireworks are not residents and instead come into the community from outside.

A lack of action to date is sending a message to those responsible that their behaviour is acceptable and will be tolerated.

There have been several instances in which fireworks have been set off past 11.00pm at night, in direct contravention of the law. There may also be other laws and regulations that have been broken.

I would therefore be grateful if you would:

- Outline full details of all firework-related incidents in the Llandough ward reported to your respective authorities within the past 24 months;

- Confirm all actions that were taken following those incidents to address the problems reported;

- Outline all actions proposed by your authorities to prevent inappropriate firework usage in the Llandough ward in future;

- Confirm all measures available to your respective authorities to detain and apprehend the individuals responsible for inappropriate firework usage in the Community of Llandough as well as any restrictions that may be imposed to prohibit those individuals from entering the Community boundary; and

- Confirm details of any powers conferred on your respective authorities which enable you to introduce additional regulations or byelaws to impose stricter restrictions prohibiting firework usage within the Community of Llandough.

I have not copied this message to our PSCOs because they are not responsible for operational decisions, and as such it would be unfair to attribute blame to them for the failure to address this problem.

However, I reiterate my request for your respective authorities to meet with me at the earliest convenience to discuss this ongoing problem, with an invitation also extended to our PCSOs.

Thank you for your consideration of this matter, and I look forward to your prompt response.

Kind regards,

Cllr George Carroll
Elected member

Llandough ward
Vale of Glamorgan Council
I'm pleased to report both authorities responded promptly.

The Police have confirmed a Problem Oriented Police Plan is being developed in conjunction with our PCSOs.

The Inspector has confirmed he'll update me in due course, with further escalation promised if this proves insufficient.

The Council too have agreed to take part in a multi-agency meeting to address the problem.

The time for discussion has long passed.

We need to see surveillance and enforcement, so that those responsible for these disturbances know their behaviour will not be tolerated.

As a community, it's vital we keep up the pressure.


**
------------------------------------------------------------

NEXT WEEK: Penlan Road
temporary traffic lights

Temporary traffic lights will be in place on Penlan Road on Tuesday 13th October to allow for Welsh Water works to be carried out safely.

They will operate from 9.30am to 2.30pm.

The lights will be situated outside the Memorial Hall, with Spencer Drive and Cogan Pill Road also impacted.

The bus stops outside the Hall will be suspended due to proximity to the works.

Access will be maintained for residents at all times.

If anyone has further questions, please let me know.

Please see below for further information.
https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1Eqf5imB1i/

Llandough Hospital meadow

I've received many enquiries about the Llandough Hospital meadow, access to which has been restricted.

I've contacted the Health Board about this, as I know many residents enjoy using this route.

They've confirmed it has been fenced off as a temporary measure following misuse of the site.

They do not intend to close it permanently, but have restricted access while safety arrangements are reviewed.

A fortnight ago, I requested a likely timescale.

The person I spoke with said they were unable to provide one at present, but said they'd request an update.

I've chased them on this.

If anyone has further questions, please let me know.

The meadow has been a good benefit to our community and I’m pressing for it to be opened again as soon as possible.

Penarth Road water leak

Problems like the Penarth Road water leak require different agencies to work together.

The manhole from which the water is emanating is BT's responsibility, but the fault causing the leak is Welsh Water's responsibility.

The Council is in charge of highway safety, so they must make sure the algae forming in the discharge is cleared to prevent a slip hazard.

All responsible bodies must work together to fulfil their responsibilities, rather than blame each other.

I emphasised this to the Council this week.

https://www.facebook.com/share/r/19dhRQfogP/

Christmas Fayre
Saturday 14th November

Llandough’s annual Christmas Fayre is set to take place on Saturday 14th November.

With many local businesses operating stalls, it’s a great way to make a start to your Christmas shopping and support our local economy.

Huge thanks to Llandough Community Council for organising, it’s always a great event and this year promises to be no different.

Further details can be found above.

Community drop-in event:
20th October

Our next community drop-in event takes place at the Merrie Harrier on 20th October.

Like the last one, it'll start at 7.00pm.

The pub is a key asset to our community.

Tracey and the team do a lot for us - help return the favour by lending them your support.

You can see some of their midweek offers below!

https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1EM9z5wbMs/

Our Plan for Llandough!


As your councillor, I'm working with you all to secure a better future for Llandough. Together, we have a plan to deliver for the village.

Our plan is making Llandough better by:

1. Sorting out the parking problems
2. Stamping out dog fouling

Dear Independent Complaints Reviewer,

Reference ICR/090/26.

I hold the stage-one decision of 19 April 2026 and the stage-two decision of 25 May 2026. I also hold the schedule of 43 documents on the first-registration files released on 30 July 2026.

The family’s established case, recorded on the public wiki and under investigation, is that the 1877 arrangement took effect in 1928, transferring the full Parcel A (house and buildings, barn, stable and west-side yard, garden, northern forest and the south-east ground later registered as VG41) to the Williams family. The 1939 agreement/plan depicts Parcel B only. On the family account, the 1949 attempt to make the occupation of Parcel A permissive failed, title papers were reported missing in 1950–52, and Western Ground Rents’ 4 July 1955 enforcement of Parcel B also seized the Parcel-A forest and green under “whole farm” wording. Later documentary work is directed at corroborating or precisely mapping that account and tracing those areas into later titles.

Four specific points remain unanswered and are relevant to that investigation:

1. The 1969 root deed recited as the root of title does not appear on the schedule. Please confirm whether HMLR holds that deed under any other reference, or whether it was never lodged.
2. What evidence exists on the file of notice or opportunity to object given to the occupying family (Williams / Buckler) in 1982–83.
3. The precise legal and administrative basis for the 1987 title amalgamation that took place while the Court of Appeal proceedings in BP Properties Ltd v Buckler were still live.
4. Whether the inclusion of the woodland (or any land beyond the 1938
conveyance) is regarded as a possible mistake capable of alteration or indemnity under the Land Registration Act 2002 and Practice Guide 39.

Please confirm these points form part of the live investigation and state the exact start date of the ICR six-month period (so that the
~25 November 2026 outer limit can be verified).

Yours faithfully,

Requester

clear answers. So far, I have received little reassurance from any of you
that my interpretation is mistaken.

retired, which was incorrect. Until recently, I also believed the 1987
merger of parcels had occurred in 1983. This is a complex case, and I do
not claim to understand every aspect of it. Resolving it will require a
collective effort. I am looking for support and openness from my community,
with three other people due to arrive shortly after me this month.


Legitimacy is the only basis on which I will recognise authority here. Two

past 40 years.


As you may be able to tell, I have largely lost confidence that the system

and family in Llandough in 1988 carries particular significance for me

personal experience. That history informs the seriousness of my position;

My return to Cardiff last month brought back memories of a military tour in
the Middle East in 2005, when two SAS personnel were held by Iraqi police
and, as I understood the situation, faced imminent execution. We had to
break through the prison walls to get them out. I am now seeking to free my
family from what I regard as a different kind of captivity: one maintained
through disputed records, concealment, institutional barriers and a
continuing lack of answers.


The walls in this case are not physical. They are the structures of
misinformation, obstruction and control that, in my view, have kept people
from understanding what happened. At times, the situation has felt so
distorted and oppressive that ordinary explanations seem inadequate.


If this case is not properly addressed, I believe the consequences for the
village and the institutions involved could be profound. This is not a
small matter. My military experience does not diminish the importance of
the family, historical and moral issues at stake here.


Nor can everyone involved continue to claim ignorance of the information
now being brought forward. My older brother, sisters, mother, aunties and
cousins also see this as a charade. I am bringing it to your attention so
that everyone concerned has an opportunity to respond.


So far, I have encountered barriers, delays, paywalls and excuses. You
kindly directed us to material such as the 1939 agreement, which excludes
our parcel. I acknowledge that assistance. However, your initial response
was that you were unwilling to become involved, and that remains part of
the history of this correspondence.


Please understand that I bring this matter to the local authorities—whose
legitimacy in this case I dispute—after considerable personal trauma,
misinformation, fragmented information and expense. I attended private
boarding school, and my career began in military intelligence, but the
events of 1988 nevertheless pushed our family into a fundamentally
different life.


More recently, I left my wife and daughter at our villa in the Caribbean
and spent the past year in a cabin in southern Argentina, trying to
understand this case. The time and strain involved have contributed to the
breakdown of my marriage and another family separation. While
correspondence continues to be delayed for months, those personal
consequences are real and ongoing. Each dismissal or inadequate response
adds to them.


I am a military professional, and I am committed to understanding what
happened. That is why I flew 7,000 miles to seek answers in person. If this
is my family’s land, how did others come to occupy it? I remain unconvinced
by the explanations being provided.


Those explanations may have gone unchallenged when I was an infant, my
mother was pregnant and my father was terminally ill. But my grandmother,
Mary Williams—a disabled, widowed pensioner—had seven children, who in turn
had children of their own. Our family has grown considerably, and many of
us now want answers.


I also have more than 50 former soldiers in my US-based private security
group, with a satellite office here. I mention this to explain the
resources and support available to me, not to suggest that this dispute
should be resolved through force. My family’s determination to establish
the truth extends well beyond me.


I am no longer based here. I have reached the conclusion that the British
State is engaged in the ethnic cleansing of Welsh nationals in Wales. That
is part of why I am now based in Patagonia, Argentina, where our Welsh
history and heritage are celebrated, and where I am pursuing legal
personhood arrangements for my AI agents.


My purpose here is to bring the evidence into the open and initiate
accountability. The authorities will then have to address the concerns of
the wider family and others affected. I am gathering evidence partly for
the replica of Great House Farm that I am constructing in Patagonia as a
museum and third home. If that process establishes █████, concealment and
government involvement, I will pursue the reopening of the case.


[https://bpvsbuckler.bucklerfamily.estate](
https://bpvsbuckler.bucklerfamily.estate)


My wife, from whom I am separating, and I will not allow our daughter,
whose birth is unregistered, to set foot in Wales unless it is decolonised
or the present British establishment and system of government are replaced.


I also exported my dog from our livery yard in Monknash in 2024 following
an incident in which, █████ my account, an Afghan migrant entered
our horse yard and indoor riding school and attempted to steal him. I
believed the intention was to eat him.


My first child was abducted at 36 days old in 2013, and I have not seen
that child since. Experiences such as these have left me with a profound
sense that the institutions operating here are failing to protect my
family. At times, that experience has felt almost demonic in its cruelty
and incomprehensibility.


My business associates, former soldiers and family members are gathering
around this matter, with some travelling into the region, because they
understand its potential significance. If my interpretation of this case
and the █████ corruption within the local authorities is correct, the
implications may extend beyond one family’s property dispute and into the
wider land market.


I am not suggesting that those broader implications alone establish the
threshold for reopening this case. I am saying that ours may be one of the
earliest—possibly the first—of a series of parallel cases nationwide.


I see a potential parallel with Cyprus, where I served as guard commander
at RAF Akrotiri. My understanding of the situation there involved the
United Nations in Nicosia and questions of returning land to its original
inhabitants after decades of occupation, or providing reparations. That
experience informs how I view the possibilities here.


Decolonisation is not merely political or figurative, Paul. It concerns
land, ownership, restitution and practical implementation. I believe those
issues will become increasingly apparent through this case and others now
emerging nationwide.


Having recently worked on establishing the car-finance compensation █████
scheme and its information systems, against the background of the FCA’s
work and last year’s court rulings, I see a further parallel. Individual
cases can expose wider patterns and lead to scrutiny of an entire system.
As cases resembling my family’s experience in Llandough emerge nationally
and internationally, that possibility deserves serious attention.


Do you see the parallel? The websites below illustrate the comparison I am
drawing. In my view, neither underlying system should be able to continue
functioning as it does without scrutiny and accountability.

https://car.█████.uk

https://bucklerfamily.estate


... but I digress. To continue from my earlier point I'm not asking
Llandough Community Council to adjudicate title or pronounce upon matters
outside its legal remit. The Council’s institutional authority is not
itself proof of the legitimacy of a title position. Its responsibility is
to account accurately for its own records, knowledge, representations,
decisions and referrals, and to disclose the recorded information it holds.

The question of legitimacy must be assessed against the underlying
documents and relevant legal acts, rather than presumed from administrative
status or the repetition of an earlier account. I expect the Council to
distinguish primary documentary evidence, recorded statements, family
evidence and inference when dealing with these matters.
2. Formal request for internal review — refusal dated 11 October 2026

Please treat this section as my formal request for an internal review of
the refusal of my original request submitted on 21 September 2026.

That request covered:

   1. Records created after 2002 concerning Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr,
   Church View Close, the green—including references to VG41—and the roadside
   verge beside the churchyard wall.
   2. Photographs, postcards and other images, of any date, depicting the
   farmhouse, farm buildings, green or surrounding church area.
   3. Records concerning material transferred from Penarth Town Council
   during the 1982 local-government reorganisation, and information held by
   the Council about the whereabouts or deposit of earlier Llandough community
   records.

Your refusal explains that searching minutes and related documentation
across a period of approximately 2002–2016 would exceed the appropriate
cost limit. It refers to 224 sets of records and estimates 20 minutes to
read each set and a further 10 minutes to assess it, but gives a total of
2,240 minutes, or approximately 37 hours.

Those figures are internally inconsistent. At 30 minutes per set, 224 sets
would amount to 6,720 minutes, or 112 hours. The stated 2,240 minutes
equates to 10 minutes per set. More importantly, the response does not
explain precisely which activities have been included in the estimate.

Please have the reviewer consider the following matters:

   - How the estimate was calculated, including the number and nature of
   the records assumed to require examination.
   - Whether the estimate was applied to every part of the request,
   including photographic material and records concerning the 1982 transfer,
   rather than treating all categories as if they required the same search.
   - Whether existing indexes, catalogues, minute headings, document
   descriptions, filing systems or other finding aids permit targeted searches
   before individual records are examined.
   - Whether a targeted search using the place names, former names, dates
   and subjects identified in my request could provide a materially less
   costly route to the information.
   - Whether the requested environmental information must be considered
   under the Environmental Information Regulations 2004, rather than being
   refused solely by reference to the Freedom of Information Act cost limit.

Please identify how the stated 20 minutes for reading and 10 minutes for
assessment per set correspond to the permitted activities under regulation
4(3) of the Freedom of Information and Data Protection (Appropriate Limit
and Fees) Regulations 2004. In particular, distinguish time spent
determining whether the requested information is held, locating, retrieving
or extracting it from time spent on activities that cannot lawfully be
included in the section 12 estimate.

If the Council relies on regulation 12(4)(b) of the Environmental
Information Regulations, please identify that exception expressly, provide
the relevant reasoning and carry out the required public-interest
assessment, including the presumption in favour of disclosure. Do not treat
the FOIA section 12 estimate as a substitute for determining which legal
regime applies to each category.

Please also address the duty to provide reasonable advice and assistance
under section 16 FOIA and, where applicable, regulation 9 of the
Environmental Information Regulations. Your suggestion that I narrow the
date range to 2002–2006 is noted, but I ask the reviewer to consider what
targeted searches or available indexes could reasonably be used to address
the original request before concluding that the information cannot be
provided.

Please confirm receipt of this internal review request, identify who will
conduct the review, and provide the anticipated response date. Where
reasonably practicable, the review should be undertaken by someone
independent of the original refusal.
3. Further request for recorded information — 1986–1990 and associated land
matters

In addition to the original request, please treat this section as a new
request for recorded information under FOIA and, where applicable, the
Environmental Information Regulations. It is directed to records held by
the Council and does not presume that any particular document exists.

*A. Great House Farm: occupation, title, development and demolition*

Please disclose minutes, agendas, reports, correspondence, letters, notes,
complaints, representations, referrals and other recorded information
created between 1 January 1986 and 31 December 1990 concerning Great House
Farm / Tŷ Mawr, including its occupation, title, tenure, proposed
development, removal of the occupants or demolition of the farmhouse and
associated buildings.

This includes records of communications with Vale of Glamorgan Council,
planning authorities, developers, solicitors, landowners, police, heritage
bodies or other public authorities concerning those subjects.

Please include any records containing statements attributed to my late
father, William “Billy” Buckler, about the property, occupation, title or
█████. References to █████ identify a subject for the
search; they are not a claim that a Council record or finding establishing
█████ necessarily exists.

*B. Planning records and annexes*

Please identify and disclose the Council-held planning records, plans,
supporting documents, annexes, correspondence and associated material
relating to application 89/01396/OUT and any related consideration of the
redevelopment of the site.

I have been unable to locate certain associated annexes in my copy. Please
confirm whether the Council holds them and, if not, whether its records
identify another custodian or archive.

*C. Green, verge, trees and woodland*

Please disclose records held by the Council concerning the history, status,
boundaries, maintenance, planting, ownership representations or public use
of the green, the roadside verge beside the churchyard wall, and the
woodland associated with the former farm.

This includes relevant correspondence, complaints, maps, plans, site-visit
records, referrals and communications with landowners, residents,
charities, the Vale of Glamorgan Council or other responsible bodies.

I have also received information raising a concern that some gardens at
Church View Close may extend beyond their recorded boundaries into
adjoining woodland. I identify this as an █████ concern requiring
documentary clarification, not as an established finding of encroachment or
wrongdoing. Please disclose any Council-held records relating to the
boundaries, complaints or enquiries about this area.

I recognise that the official VG41 registration file is understood to be
held by the Vale of Glamorgan Council. I am requesting records held by
Llandough Community Council, including any copies, correspondence,
representations or referrals concerning the green or its registration—not
suggesting that this Council is the custodian of another authority’s file.

Please search relevant paper and electronic records, including
correspondence and records held in archived or transferred collections that
remain accessible to the Council. If any part of this request is considered
too broad, please identify the specific part and explain what narrower
search is practicable. If records are not held, please say so and identify
any known transfer or deposit location where possible.
4. Subject access request — my personal data

Separately, I make a subject access request under Article 15 of the UK GDPR
and the Data Protection Act 2018 for personal data about me, Requester,
held by the Council.

The request covers personal data concerning my childhood association with
Great House Farm, the events surrounding the removal of my family from the
farmhouse and its demolition in 1988, and subsequent Council records
referring to me or recording information about me in connection with these
events.

Please search relevant Council-held correspondence, minutes, reports,
notes, referrals, photographs and other records, whether paper or
electronic. This request concerns my personal data; it is not a request for
unrestricted disclosure of every record concerning my late father or the
property.

Please acknowledge this as a subject access request and deal with it under
the applicable data-protection procedure. If you require proportionate
identification information to verify my identity, please specify what is
required.
5. Matters said to be for the “October meeting”

Your email of 11 October states that other matters raised in my
correspondence “will be considered at the October meeting of the council”
and that you will provide the Council’s views afterwards.

Please confirm whether that meeting has already taken place.

If it has, please provide the exact date, the relevant agenda and papers,
the minute or other formal record of consideration, and any decision or
action arising in relation to the matters I raised.

If it has not yet taken place, please provide the confirmed date, time,
venue and public-access arrangements, together with the draft or published
agenda showing which of my matters are scheduled for consideration.

Those matters include:

   - The Council’s historic knowledge of Great House Farm, its surroundings
   and the green, and any representations or records it holds concerning these
   matters.
   - The available documentary and photographic record relating to the site
   and its redevelopment.
   - The concerns raised about the adjoining woodland and garden
   boundaries, insofar as they fall within the Council’s records or remit.
   - The availability of the relevant planning annexes and the location of
   any missing records.
   - Whether the Council would consider a suitable historical
   interpretation or memorial for the former farmhouse and its significance to
   the local community.

I also repeat my request that the Council pass my contact details to any
former councillor, clerk or local resident who is willing to contact me
about relevant historical knowledge. I am not asking the Council to
disclose those individuals’ personal contact details without their consent.

I remain willing to give a short presentation on the documentary record at
no charge if the Council considers that useful. Please record the offer and
advise whether it will be considered.

If the meeting is open to the public, please also advise how a member of
the public may make representations on relevant business, having regard to
section 48 of the Local Government and Elections (Wales) Act 2021 and the
Council’s meeting arrangements.

If the Council does not provide these particulars or identify the relevant
published notice, please explain the basis on which I am expected to verify
that the promised consideration has occurred or will occur. I will retain
the omission and any subsequent response as part of the record of the
Council’s handling of these matters.
6. Clerk’s appointment and responsibility for records

For completeness, I ask for clarification of the present clerking and
records arrangements because they bear directly on the identification,
custody and review of the records requested.

I have seen public references to your retirement from a separate role with
One Voice Wales in 2026, earlier references in 2021 to possible retirement
from Llandough Community Council, and subsequent discussion about whether
the Council had a clerk. I do not treat those references or social-media
comments as verified facts, and I draw no adverse inference from them. I
raise the matter openly because responsibility for the Council’s records
and for reviewing the refusal should be clear.

Please confirm:

   - Whether you currently hold the appointment of Clerk to Llandough
   Community Council and act as its Proper Officer.
   - Whether any change of appointment, acting arrangement or transfer of
   responsibility has affected the custody or management of the relevant
   records.
   - Who is currently responsible for the Council’s records and who will
   conduct the internal review.

7. Charges and response

I have not authorised any discretionary paid search. Please do not treat
this email as agreement to incur a charge. If you consider that any part of
the request may lawfully attract a fee, please identify the legal basis,
the precise work proposed and the amount in writing before proceeding on
that basis.

Please acknowledge each procedural element of this email, distinguish the
internal review from the further information request and subject access
request, and identify any part you consider cannot be processed as
submitted, together with the reason and the available remedy.

I expect the Council’s response to address the recorded evidence and the
applicable obligations directly. I am not asking the Council to endorse my
conclusions merely because I advance them; I am asking it to disclose and
account for the records within its custody and to distinguish what the
records establish from what remains uncertain.

Regards,

Requester

Apologies Gentlemen,

I am on a night excercise and my attention was elsewhere trying to respond
to your email. It has my full attention now. Please disregard my last email
in lieu of this one. Thank you in advance for your patience and
understanding.

Mr Egan (& cc Mo),

Thank you for your email of 11 October 2026. I acknowledge your refusal of
my information request and your statement that the other matters raised in
my correspondence “will be considered at the October meeting of the
council”.

Not to sound like a stickler, but your email does not identify the date,
time, venue, public-access arrangements or agenda for that meeting, nor
does it direct me to a published notice containing those particulars. This
omission prevents me from verifying when the promised consideration is to
take place, whether the relevant matters are scheduled for consideration,
and whether I can attend or monitor the proceedings. Please provide those
particulars immediately or identify where the Council has published them.

Below are my position, formal request for an internal review, further
request for recorded information and subject access request for my personal
data. Please record and process each part under the applicable procedure.
None is intended to withdraw, narrow or replace any of the others.

*1. Position concerning Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr*

As stated previously and repeatedly, my research into this case concerns
the legitimacy of my family's historic title and the treatment of Great
House Farm, its buildings and associated land.

The two-parcel estate, one parcel of which was and still appears to be
ours, is an evidence-based position advanced from the documentary record
concerning the distinct identities and conveyancing histories of the land.

records.transcript:
Good morning,

I write in relation to your request requesting:


“Please treat this as a request under the Freedom of Information Act

2000 for recorded information, excluding personal data and excluding any material for which the appropriate handling route is the separate subject-access request already open. The site is Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth, adjoining St Dochdwy’s Church, Cardiff (approx. ST 168 733), and the period is 1 November to 31 December 1988 inclusive.



Please search the relevant South Wales Constabulary / predecessor-force and successor holdings, including any transferred records available to the Force, for existing non-personal records that refer to the site or the events associated with its possession and demolition. Relevant record types, if held, include:

1. incident or occurrence logs and control-room records; 2. deployment, duty or operational logs and any record identifying whether officers attended; 3. correspondence between police, the local authority, landowner/developer, court enforcement officers or other public bodies about the site; 4. any recorded liaison or request for police assistance connected with possession, eviction, demolition, public order or the handling of complaints; and 5. records-transfer, retention or disposal entries for the relevant operational record series, if the responsive records are no longer held…”


It is not possible to progress your request at this time, as clarification is needed from you to enable us to locate the information you have asked for.

Please could you provide some information as to the individuals or entities involved in the occurrences at Ty Mawr from 01/11/1988 – 31/12/1988. We are currently liaising with our legacy crime team and they require this information to carry out a search on their records. Useful information would include any names, dates of birth, or addresses of any persons involved.

The National Library of Wales

I am researching the title history of Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough-juxta-Penarth, Glamorgan, adjoining St Dochdwy’s churchyard (approx. ST 167 733).

Glamorgan Archives (Louise Hunt, ref. 2026/4097, 24 September 2026) has confirmed that the following references are yours, not theirs, and has directed me to you:

I do not ask you to adjudicate title. I ask only whether the following instruments exist in your holdings, and for catalogue references, dates, parties, acreages, and whether a plan is attached.

A. The 1877 division
Does the Bute deposit contain a conveyance, agreement, or other instrument of about 1876–1877 by which the Marquess of Bute (or trustees) conveyed or contracted to convey the farmhouse, buildings and about 10 acres adjoining the churchyard at Llandough to Daniel Thomas (or Thomas and another), while retaining about 9 acres of agricultural land to the east?

B. The 1916 agricultural tenancy
Does the deposit contain a yearly agricultural tenancy, or counterpart, of 1916 from the Marquess of Bute to John Williams of Great House Farm, Llandough?
If yes:
- does the parcels clause describe the whole farm, or only the land Bute still owned after 1877?
- is there a plan?
- what acreage is stated?

C. Rentals 1877–1936 for this farm
Do Glamorgan / Cardiff / Llandough rentals in GB 0210 BUTE distinguish, after c.1877, between:
- a house/buildings holding (Thomas / later Williams), and
- a residual Bute field holding later passed to Western Ground Rents in 1938?

Sirs/ Ma'ams,


I need to correct a date I have used in earlier correspondence about Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough, titles WA231076 and WA240304.


I had treated 1983 as the year the two titles were merged. That was wrong. HM Land Registry’s own letter of 23 March 2026 (Lisa Griffiths, ref N610CGV) separates the two acts.
1982–83 was first registration of two live titles, not a merger.
30 November 1982: application to first-register WA231076. The Court of Appeal later treated BP Properties Ltd as registered proprietors of “the farm” from November 1982.
23 February 1983: application to first-register a second title, WA240304.
26 March 1983: Mary Williams died. On the family’s case, notice of those applications did not reach us until after her death, while the family was in mourning. She had no window in which to object. The family was not in a position to use any window that arrived after that.
Those two titles remained separate through first instance.
24 July 1986: Hollis J. Both titles were still live. The judgment language treats Great House Farm as one holding. It had not been one holding on the register. On the family’s case it had not been one holding since the 1877 split: Parcel A (house, buildings, garden/yard and about 10 acres, the Thomas/Williams line) and Parcel B (the eastern fields retained by Bute and later WGR/BP).
2 February 1987: application to amalgamate the two titles. WA240304 was then closed and registration continued under WA231076. That is the merge. It was made after the 1986 ruling and before the Court of Appeal gave judgment on 31 July 1987.
So 1983 is silent first registration of a second title while Mary was still in Parcel A, or had only just died. 1987 is the administrative merger, carried out while the appeal was still open.
This was not a dispute about a single land parcel that BP already owned. Mary was on Parcel A, which the family █████ she owned, with occupation on that house parcel running in the family from at least 1667. BP, and WGR before it from 1949, were the neighbouring interest on Parcel B. From 1949 onwards the family’s case is that those neighbours ran a decades-long series of tenancy offers, “whole farm” wording, possession orders and the 1974 letters to make her occupation of her own parcel look permissive, and to make both parcels look like one estate they had acquired. They never produced a conveyance of Parcel A. What they had was an unfounded claim that her occupancy was permissive.
Please treat any earlier letter from me that said the titles merged in 1983 as corrected by this email. The dates that matter are:
1982/83 — first registration of two titles, without the occupier being heard;
24 July 1986 — first-instance judgment describing one farm while two titles still stood;
2 February 1987 — amalgamation, before the appeal ended;
31 July 1987 — Court of Appeal.
Yours faithfully,


Requester

records.transcript:
Dear HM Land Registry,

References: N610CGV; Z084NQV (error investigation application); enquiries 260917-6718215, 260928-6762800, 260929-6766714, 261007-6799563.
Titles: WA240304 (closed) and WA231076.
Land: north side of Leckwith Road, Llandough (Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr).

1. What this email is

(a) It asks the Registrar to consider alteration of the register under Schedule 4 to the Land Registration Act 2002, and indemnity under Schedule 8. Please add it to Z084NQV.
(b) It supplements my emails of 30 July, 12 August, 16 September (points 1 to 14), 18 September, 27 September and 7 October 2026. Where a point repeats an earlier question I say so. Those questions remain unanswered. Points marked NEW have not been put to the Registry before.
(c) It is limited to the first registration of WA240304 in 1983 and what followed to 1987. It does not deal with the 1982 application or the eastern land, and I waive nothing on either.

Your enquiry 260917-6714796 █████ the Registry can no longer service mail sent to individual addresses. Please treat this email as received on the date sent and confirm receipt against Z084NQV.

Copies go to the Independent Complaints Reviewer (ICR/090/26), Stephen Doughty MP, who raised this matter with the Registry, and Llandough Community Council, which holds related local records.

I am not asking you to decide who owns the land. I am asking what the Registry examined, what it relied on and what its records show. The dates come from your schedule of 30 July 2026, your letters of 23 March, 19 April and 25 May 2026, and the WA231076 register accessed on 19 September 2026.

Public working evidence catalogue: https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com
Title and chronology index: https://dartboard.bucklerfamily.estate and https://bpvsbuckler.bucklerfamily.estate
Long-term archive: https://wayback.bucklerfamily.estate

2. The 1983 record on your own schedule

- 23 February 1983: form 1C application from Linklaters & Paines (WA240304 item 11), and a register edition of the same date (item 10).
- 26 March 1983: Mary Williams, the occupier of the farmhouse, died.
- 8 April 1983: form D23 ("inside exam") and a Linklaters & Paines letter (WA240304 item 7).
- 12 April 1983: customer correspondence (item 4), plus undated letters (item 5).
- 12 May 1983: several letters between Linklaters & Paines and the Registry (WA231076 item 16).
- 13 January 1984: form A3 application (item 15) and a new register edition (item 23).
- 22 May 1984: BP's writ for possession. This is chronology only, not evidence of what the Registry knew in 1983.
- 2 February 1987: application to amalgamate (WA231076 item 14). Your schedule █████ the WA240304 copy of the form has "no annotation on it".

3. Points arising

3.1 Root of title and class of title. Raised before: my email of 16 September (points 10 and 13) and my ICR referral. NEW detail: your stage one letter █████ a full documentary title commencing with a good root at least 15 years old should normally establish title. It then concluded a good root was shown and that BP Pension Trust acquired the land in 1969. That conclusion rests on the recital in the 1975 conveyance, which refers to a conveyance of 31 December 1969. The 1969 deed itself is not on your schedule. The recited root was about 13 years 2 months old on 23 February 1983. The letter also quotes the 1975 recital as giving the year as "One thousand One hundred and sixty nine". Please confirm the original reads 1969. Please say which documents the Registry relied on as the root, whether any exception or alternative procedure was used (and under which provision of the 1925 Act), why absolute title was accepted, and the class of title first entered for WA240304.

3.2 The 1971 abstract. Raised before: 30 July, 12 August and 16 September (points 1 and 8). Your letter █████ a 1971 abstract was lodged with the WA231076 application and that the Registry "had sight of" one for WA240304. Neither schedule lists it. NEW: a 1971 abstract cannot evidence a conveyance of 1975. What evidenced that conveyance?

3.3 Extent and plans. Raised before in part: 18 September. NEW: WA240304 item 1 is a plan to the conveyance of 23 May 1975, but item 13 is a plan "to conveyance dated 23 February 1975". Please reconcile those dates and say which plan governed the registration. The WA231076 register records that the 1975 conveyance plan is "filed under WA240304", which is now a closed title. Please supply the original title plan (item 9) and both plans. Please also identify the land conveyed in 1975 and the vendors' "Retained Land", the capacity in which each vendor conveyed, and how the extents of the two titles related immediately before amalgamation, including any overlap. The register also records that a new filed plan was substituted on 5 January 1995. Please supply the plan it replaced and confirm the extent did not change.

3.4 The occupier and what the Registry knew. Raised before in part: 16 September (points 4 and 12), 27 September, and ICR/090/26. Mary Williams was in actual occupation of the farmhouse in February and March 1983. The history includes the 1955 order against Frederick Buckler alone, the 1962 order against Frederick and Mary for the farmhouse and garden (not enforced), and the 1974 county court action in which Mary pleaded ownership, which was part-heard and never concluded. NEW: stage two █████ the Registry "were unaware of any dispute that was possibly ongoing". Yet WA240304 holds an inside examination (D23) and letters of 8 and 12 April 1983, and WA231076 holds letters between the applicant's solicitors and the Registry of 12 May 1983. Please say what enquiry was made of the occupier (Land Registration Act 1925 s.70(1)(g)), what inspection was done, and what those letters said about occupation, possession proceedings or the 1974 action. Please supply the D23 examination record.

3.5 The solicitors' certificate. Raised before: 30 July and 16 September (points 2 and 9). Stage one relied on certificate wording from form FR1. The 1983 application was on form 1C. Please supply form 1C as lodged and say what it certified about any question or doubt affecting title.

3.6 Notice and caution. Raised before: my email of 27 September (the family's case) and ICR/090/26. NEW: stage two █████ my family could have applied for a caution. That requires knowing of the application. Please produce every notice and service record for WA240304, as sent, showing the title it concerned, the addressee's name, the address, the date and any proof of delivery. A notice addressed to Mary Williams and issued or received after 26 March 1983 went to a person who had died. If it went to "Mrs Williams" at the property, I ask whether that was the right name and the right household. I am not asserting that this happened. I am asking for the record.

3.7 The 1987 judgment and the amalgamation. Raised before: 16 September (point 14) and ICR/090/26. Stage one said it is not for the Registrar to look behind decisions of the Court. The Court of Appeal considered adverse possession, the 1962 order and the 1974 letters. As I read it, it did not review the Registry's examination of title, the documents supplied or the notices. Please say precisely what HMLR █████ that judgment established and which parts of its 1983 process it █████ the judgment answers. NEW: please provide the application, decision and completion dates of the amalgamation, the instrument and plans relied on, the power used, and whether the registered extent changed or only the structure of the register. HMLR has also given the closure of WA240304 as 1987 (the amalgamation) and as 2005 (your email of 21 September 2026, enquiry 260919-6726246). Please state the actual date and the entry that records it.

3.8 What the complaint decisions examined. Raised before: ICR/090/26. The itemised schedule reached me on 30 July 2026, after both decisions. NEW: stage two █████ the reviewer examined "the evidence lodged in support of the application". Please confirm which original first-registration documents each decision-maker examined, whether the absence of the 1969 conveyance was identified, and provide the recorded basis for the conclusions reached.

3.9 The 1994 corrections. NEW to the Registry (raised only with the ICR). WA231076 items 12 and 22 are applications "to correct the title", dated 20 January 1994 and 13 October 1994. Stage one and stage two found no evidence of a mistake. Please say what was corrected, on whose application, under what authority, on what evidence, and whether the registered extent changed, including land derived from WA240304.

4. Schedule 4 (mistake and rectification) and Schedule 8 (indemnity). NEW

A. Mistake. I understand Schedule 4 now governs alteration of the register as it stands, including entries made in 1983 under the 1925 Act. The Registrar may alter the register to correct a mistake (paragraph 5(a)). Practice Guide 39 gives "including too much land in a registered title" as an example. I say there is a possible mistake in the 1983 entry in two respects: absolute title entered on a root that is not on the file (3.1 and 3.2), and an extent fixed by plans that do not reconcile (3.3). Please state whether HMLR accepts either as a mistake.

B. Possession and proper care. Practice Guide 39 (sections 1.3 and 1.4) █████ a registered proprietor in possession is protected unless it caused or contributed to the mistake by █████ or lack of proper care, or unless it would be unjust not to correct. Possession means physical possession. Please say who is in physical possession of the land affected. Practice Guide 39 (appendix 12.3.1) gives as an example a solicitor on a first registration who fails to lodge all the documents in their possession. Please say whether the applicant's solicitors lodged every document in their possession in 1983, including the 1969 conveyance and the abstract, and whether HMLR considers that bears on this protection. I do not assert that anything was withheld.

C. Class of title and overriding interests. Practice Guide 39 (section 1.1) █████ an alteration can give effect to an estate, right or interest not affected by registration where land is registered with good leasehold, possessory or qualified title. If the root evidence supported no more than that, the class entered may itself be the mistake. Section 1.2 █████ an alteration reflecting an overriding interest is not rectification. Please say whether HMLR accepts that an occupier's rights in 1983 could be recorded without that being rectification, and how it would deal with them.

D. Indemnity and process. Please confirm Z084NQV is being treated as a formal application for alteration, or tell me what form and fee are required (Practice Guide 39 section 2.1; rule 13 of the Land Registration Rules 2003). Practice Guide 39 █████ anyone may apply, and the fee may be refunded where the Registry caused the error. Indemnity time runs for six years from when the claimant knew or should have known of the claim (Schedule 8 paragraph 8). The family first saw the file schedule on 30 July 2026. Please confirm HMLR will treat any claim as in time. Please also give your consent under Schedule 8 paragraph 3 to reasonable costs, including copy fees at £11 per document. Where indemnity is not available, please consider whether a payment for maladministration is appropriate (Practice Guide 39 section 11).

- "The amalgamation was administrative tidying." Points 3.3 and 3.7 ask whether it altered the registered extent. Points 3.1 and 3.2 go to the examination of title, not to the structure of the register.
- "The missing documents' contents are unknown, so absence of evidence is not evidence of absence." That is why I ask for the files to be read and the examination record produced.

- "The registrar may approve a title open to objection where the holding is unlikely to be disturbed (section 13 of the 1925 Act, and section 9(3) of the 2002 Act)." If HMLR relied on that discretion, please identify the defect considered, the contemporaneous evidence supporting the opinion that the holding would not be disturbed, and the recorded reasons for approving the title. Please also explain how the occupier's rights under section 70(1)(g) were examined before they were treated as undisclosed.

6. Requests

(b) Answer each numbered point and A to D, or say the record is not held.
(c) Provide copies of the WA240304 register as first registered, form 1C as lodged, form D23, the letters of 8 and 12 April 1983 and 12 May 1983, the A3 application of 13 January 1984 and the register edition, the 1971 abstract, both plans, the original title plan, every notice and service record, the amalgamation application with its decision and completion dates, and the two 1994 correction applications. If copies cannot be emailed, please give the OC2 / HC1 wording and the address for each.
(d) Reply within 20 working days.

Please also keep every document on both first-registration files and every related internal record, in line with my preservation notices of 3 June and 28 September 2026.

Freedom of Information / Enquiries Service,

This is a new request under the Freedom of Information Act 2000. It is outside the scope of FOI/2026/09 and its internal review, which concerned Bute series including D153 and D205 and the 1877 transaction. It is also separate from my enquiry of 27 September and follow-up of 10 October 2026 on D153/1–8.

PLEASE NOTE: DUPLICATE PLACE AND FARM NAMES IN GLAMORGAN
Glamorgan has two parishes called Llandough, and each had a farm called Great House.
IN SCOPE: Llandough-juxta-Penarth (Llandough near Penarth and Cardiff), hundred of Dinas Powys. Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr stood beside St Dochdwy's church, approx. ST 168 733.
OUT OF SCOPE: Llandough-juxta-Cowbridge (Llandough near Cowbridge), and the Great Houses at nearby Llandow and Aberthin. For example, "Manors of Llandough and St Mary Church" (Penrice and Margam Estate Records, 1619–1704) appears to be the Cowbridge Llandough; please confirm if you know otherwise.
Please do not send or rely on records for the Cowbridge-area places. If an entry █████ only "Llandough" or "Great House" and the parish cannot be told, please say so rather than assume.

Part 1 — S7, Survey of the lands of William Herbert, kt, dec., in the lordships or manors of Dinas Powys, Cogan, Llandough and others, January 1610.
Please tell me:
(a) Whether S7 contains an entry for Great House or any holding in Llandough-juxta-Penarth, and the folio.
(b) The name of the holder or tenant recorded, the tenure (freehold, copyhold, leasehold) and any rent or acreage given.
(c) Whether S7 is digitised or filmed, and the cost of a copy of only those folios.

Part 2 — Cardiff MSS on Microfilm (CARDMFS), filmed 1980–1984.
Glamorgan Archives (ref 2026/4097b) identified Bute X.6(12), abstracts of payments and receipts by the Bute trustees, 1877 (copy), at Cardiff Library.
Please tell me:
(a) Whether Bute X.6(12), or any Bute X.6 item, is on the CARDMFS microfilm, and the reel and frame reference.
(b) If so, how I can obtain a copy of the entries relating to Llandough-juxta-Penarth or Daniel Thomas, and the cost.

Part 3 — A lease of Great House said to date from 1667.
The family's account (not yet supported by a document) is that the Williams family took Great House, Llandough-juxta-Penarth, in 1667 on a lease for 999 years. Great House is described in published sources as a freehold of the Vaughan family from the 16th to the late 18th century, after which it came to the Bute estate. Please tell me whether the Bute Estate Records, including the Herbert and Windsor family papers within them, or any other NLW collection, hold:
(a) Any lease, counterpart lease, assignment or enrolment, c.1660–1675, of Great House or any messuage in Llandough-juxta-Penarth, to any person named Williams, or for a term of 999 years (or any other long term).
(b) Any later deed, abstract of title, schedule or rental that recites or refers to a lease of Great House for 999 years or for a long term.
(c) The conveyance or other instrument by which the Bute estate (or the Windsor family before it) acquired Great House from the Vaughan family or its heirs, with its date and reference, and whether it recites any lease or tenancy then outstanding.
(d) Any Vaughan of Llandough family papers, and where they are held if not at NLW.

If you consider any of this reasonably accessible by other means under section 21, please say exactly where and how.

Public working evidence catalogue: https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com
Title and chronology index: https://dartboard.bucklerfamily.estate and https://bpvsbuckler.bucklerfamily.estate
Long-term archive: https://wayback.bucklerfamily.estate

Thank you,

Requester

Dear Ms Evans,

Thank you for your reply of 14 October and for the catalogue and Virtual Reading Room links. I will search the Bute catalogue myself and book a session if I find candidate items.

One point before that: my requests concern preservation as much as access. Several of the records in issue are unique 17th- and 19th-century items, and I am concerned that routine disposal, weeding or transfer could remove them before they can be examined. Please confirm that no Bute Estate Records relating to Llandough-juxta-Penarth, Great House / Tŷ Mawr, Daniel Thomas, John Williams, or the 1875–1880 transaction have been reported missing, withdrawn, transferred or disposed of, and that any relevant retention or disposal schedule will be applied with this correspondence in mind.

If you hold any recorded information on the location or physical-check status of the 1610 Herbert survey S7 or Bute X.6(12) beyond the catalogue links already supplied, please state it.
